description:
Fellowship means sharing a common purpose, not merely spending time together. Wesam Saad turns to the church’s unity, warning that gossip and divisive teaching can feed pride and a desire for control. He distinguishes handling minor doctrinal differences responsibly from remaining silent about a different gospel. Allegiance to Christ comes first; preserving unity does not require accepting teaching that undermines the gospel.

Ephesians 4:2–3 gives the positive response: humility, gentleness, patience and bearing with one another in love. Humility regards others as more important without retreating into self-pity or refusing to serve. Gentleness restrains the ability to wound, so that truth is spoken to restore rather than crush. Patience accepts the cost of dealing with imperfect people instead of answering hurt with retaliation.

Wesam stresses that the one-another commands must be practised among the members of a local congregation. Kindness elsewhere cannot replace love for those alongside us. He applies this to guarded speech, willingness to forgive and sharing another person’s joy even when one’s own circumstances are painful. Such unity requires dying to self and finding satisfaction in Christ, rather than allowing disappointed preferences to govern relationships. These practical responsibilities prepare the way for a fuller examination of the one-another commands.

questions.question: How is fellowship defined at the start of the study?
questions.answer: It is participation with others in a common purpose, described as communion with fellow believers and with God. The discussion therefore moves beyond social contact to the shared life and unity of a congregation.

questions.question: Why does Wesam warn particularly about gossip and divisive teaching?
questions.answer: He describes them as destructive to the church’s unity and connects their appeal with pride and control. A person can feel superior by damaging another’s reputation or by promoting teaching in a way that places themselves above others.

questions.question: How should minor doctrinal differences be distinguished from another gospel?
questions.answer: Wesam describes discussing a minor conviction honestly with elders and avoiding a divisive campaign in a Bible-believing congregation. He sharply distinguishes that from a false gospel, which should be opposed rather than protected by silence, because allegiance to Christ comes first.

questions.question: What qualities does Ephesians 4:2–3 require for preserving unity?
questions.answer: It calls for humility, gentleness and patience, expressed in bearing with one another in love and diligence to preserve the Spirit’s unity in peace. The study emphasises embracing these qualities as well as refusing the practices that divide.

questions.question: How does the teacher distinguish humility from self-pity?
questions.answer: Humility considers others more important and moves towards serving them. It is not saying that one is too insignificant to contribute. Wesam describes moving confidence away from oneself and placing it in God, rather than using unworthiness as a reason to withdraw.

questions.question: What does gentleness mean when another person is wrong?
questions.answer: It is restraint rather than weakness. Wesam says a person may be able to win an argument or hurt another badly, but should speak with care, honour and a desire to help the person draw closer to Christ. Gentleness does not mean never correcting sin.

questions.question: How is patience connected with bearing with one another?
questions.answer: The study describes patience as enduring hurt without retaliation while dealing with imperfect people. It works with humility and gentleness, so that a believer continues seeking another’s good rather than insisting that unity is possible only with people who have no faults.

questions.question: Why does the local meaning of one another matter?
questions.answer: The command is addressed to the people who belong together in that congregation. Wesam’s family illustration shows that treating someone elsewhere kindly does not discharge a responsibility towards the brother or sister one is neglecting at home in the church.

questions.question: What practical responses does the closing application call for?
questions.answer: Believers should avoid damaging speech, speak sensitively when raising an offence, be ready to forgive and rejoice with others even when their own circumstances hurt. Wesam connects these responses with denying self and finding identity, delight and satisfaction in Christ.
